steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or lightly coat with cooking spray.

Separate crescent dough into triangles; cut each triangle in half lengthwise to create narrower strips. Place one cocktail sausage on the wide end of each strip. If using cheese, add a small piece underneath the sausage. Roll up tightly.
Place rolls, seam-side down, on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown and puffed, about 12 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pigs in a Blanket
raw_recipe.description: These pigs in a blanket are made with cocktail sausages wrapped in crescent roll dough for a fun and delicious holiday party appetizer in 30 minutes.

review.reviewBody: This is a wonderful, fun recipe to make. We only made a few minor adjustments from the original recipe: We preheated the oven to 400 degrees instead of 350 degrees. We also used two packages of cocktail weiners (Li'l Smokies) and 4 tubes of Pillsbury Crescent Rolls instead of biscuit dough. We tried the biscuit dough last year but after using the crescent dough this year we found we like that a lot better. Make sure you cut the crescent rolls in half first before you wrap them around the Li'l Smokies. We omitted the cheese and baked them on a "greased" cookie sheet. These taste best fresh out of the oven as then tend to get kind of soft the next day if refrigerated in a Ziploc.

I make these for a fun dinner night and serve them with Pork & Beans... Instead of using pre made biscuits, substitute with Bisquick Gluten free (follow the biscuit recipe).Also include 1 cup of finely shredded sharp cheddar cheese with onion and garlic powder. (approximately) 1 teaspoon of each to the dough. Preheat the oven to 350 and spray the baking sheet with canola oil. Bake for 10 to 15 minutes and serve with a Sriracha ketchup sauce for dipping. Pork and Beans on the side.

Sriracha Ketchup sauce:
1 cup of ketchup and 1/4 cup of sriracha hot sauce, mix and I suggest serving the dip at room temperature or warm for 30 to 45 seconds on medium power in the microwave . We prefer to dip a warm item into a warm sauce.

Pork and Beans:
1 slice of bacon cooked well and break up into small pieces, 1/2 of small onion finely diced and saute in with the bacon until tender, add 1, 16 ounce can of pork and beans (used Publix brand) and add 1/4 cup of BBQ sauce (used Sweet Baby Rays). You wont be disappointed!
I use little smokies instead - pan fried to release some of the oils first. Roll the dough out thin, since they do puff out. Hubs love to dip in mustard or ketchup.

As written, I'd say this recipe would be maybe 3 1/2 stars...I mean, its just fancy hot dogs, and we really find using biscuit dough to be too overpowering and, well, dough-y! my lil tweak to take these buggars over the top is to use the Pillsbury Honey Butter crescents!!! their lightly sweet flavor combined with the savory saltiness of the hot dogs is a taste sensation! My son says I've "ruined" all other pigs in a blanket now for him because they just don't measure up to these. Lol. I also cut the triangles in half and set the oven at 375, and they are perfect- and gone within minutes- every time!

Well, it's not a party without these little bite size treats! Who knew such few ingredients could produce something so good! I use Pillbury crescent rolls and cut them with a pizza cutter to make things easy. I always spray a bit of Pam so nothing sticks. I heat my oven to 375 vs. 350 for baking. I serve these with a variety of dipping sauces - bbq, honey mustard, spicy brown mustard, dijon, apricot jam mixed with a bit of bbq sauce -the possibilites are endless! One thing is for sure, these are always a hit at get togethers and you're guests will definitely thank you!

I’ve made a version of this for decades. (I’m old. LOL). I use crescent rolls and place the hot dogs or sausages on the wide end and roll them up with the narrow end at the top. I make a spicy ketchup dipping sauce and Voila Yum. Kids love them. So do my great grandkids now.

Quick and easy to make. I too subbed crescent rolls dough for the biscuit, cutting the crescent triangles in half. I used regular length beef hot dogs and cut them in half too. Then cut a sliver through the hot dog half and stuffed with the cheeses... some with mozzarella, some cheddar and some mixed. Then I wrap the stuffed hot dog halves in the triangle to baked at 375. The beef hot dogs I think add a lot more flavor but that’s just my personal preference. Nice party snack! They go quickly!!

I made several changes to this recipe and it turned out a little fancier! I took some onion and diced them up really tiny to tuck in beside the hotdog while rolling them up with the dough. Instead of canned biscuit dough, I took frozen biscuits (which tend to brown better, and are more crisp) and let them come to room temperature or until doughy and soft. I used some flour for dusting and rolled them out and wrapped it up! Good with warm mustard.

I cooked the little smokies in a fry pan with maple syrup, chipotle hot sauce and a pat of butter. Allow syrup mixture to carmelize and cool sausages slightly before rolling them in the crescent roll. More of a breakfast flavor.

Easy and delicious! Before baking, I combined butter and garlic powder and brushed the tops with the mixture. Everything else as directed. Sooo good! We made fake freddy's sauce: ketchup, mayo and dill pickle juice. It worked, but I liked honey mustard a bit more.

I’ve made *these* for many, many yrs for my son’s classes! Except I’ve always used crescent rolls cut in 1/3ds and rolled around “lil smokies “ . Sometimes added silvers of cheddar or jack cheese. Each and every child (up to young adults) devoured them as fast as they could. Teachers too! I never had any to take home.!
I bake mine at 375. I also cut each crescent triangle into 3 pieces. Always a hit and so easy!
We been making these since my kids were little. Now I make them for my grandkids.
Turned out great, I did half with cheese.
One kid ate the hot dog, one kid ate the dough. Nobody complained. Definitely a win
Great recipe for kids! My 5 year old grandson helped me make them and had a lot of fun doing it. I would definitely set the oven to 375 or 400 because at 350, they took twice as long to get golden.

My late mother used to make these but instead of the biscuit though she used crescent rolls and that's what I'm going to do for my son but cooking time was the same cheese amount was the same everything was the same. And as far as cheese goes it's whatever you like
